statement: Where a patentee (or persons making, offering for sale, or selling a patented article under the patentee) fails to mark patented articles as § 287(a) prescribes, no damages are recoverable in an infringement action except on proof that the infringer was notified of the infringement and continued to infringe thereafter, and then only for infringement occurring after such notice; filing an infringement action itself constitutes notice (35 U.S.C. § 287(a)).
caveat: The marking limitation applies where there are patented articles to mark; assertions of method claims or by patentees with nothing to mark sit outside § 287(a)'s bar, and damages remain separately time-limited to six years before the complaint by 35 U.S.C. § 286. Whether a particular demand letter constitutes sufficient notice is a case-specific legal question.
